steps: Resuscitate (airway, breathing, circulation); treat hypoglycaemia and give thiamine where relevant.
Identify the toxidrome; contact a poisons service (e.g. TOXBASE/Poison Centre) for agent-specific advice.
Decontamination (activated charcoal) only if early, airway-safe and appropriate agent.
Specific antidotes where indicated (naloxone, NAC, flumazenil caution, etc.); supportive monitoring.
Enhanced elimination/dialysis for selected toxins; psychiatric assessment after medical stabilisation.

drugRefs.dose: 0.4–2 mg, repeat every 2–3 min; infusion if recurrent
drugRefs.freq: titrated to adequate respiration (not full consciousness)
drugRefs.why: Reverses opioid-induced respiratory depression; titrate to breathing to avoid precipitating acute withdrawal.

drugRefs.dose: 150 mg/kg over 1 h, then 50 mg/kg over 4 h, then 100 mg/kg over 16 h (21-h regimen)
drugRefs.why: Replenishes glutathione and prevents hepatotoxicity in paracetamol overdose; most effective within 8 h.

drugRefs.freq: single dose if within ~1 h and airway protected
drugRefs.why: Adsorbs many ingested toxins; only if early, appropriate agent and airway safe (aspiration risk).

drugRefs.dose: 100 mg (higher, e.g. 500 mg, if Wernicke suspected)
drugRefs.freq: before/with glucose in alcohol-dependent or malnourished
drugRefs.why: Prevents Wernicke's encephalopathy; give with/before glucose in at-risk patients.

drugRefs.dose: 200 mcg IV over 15 s, then 100 mcg at 1-min intervals (max ~1 mg)
drugRefs.why: Reverses benzodiazepine sedation but can precipitate seizures/arrhythmia in dependence or co-ingested proconvulsants — rarely used, seek poisons advice.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Poisoning and Drug Overdose
TOXBASE / National Poisons Information Service guidance
Position Papers of the American Academy of Clinical Toxicology / EAPCCT (decontamination)

decision.label: Resuscitate; antidote by toxidrome + poisons advice

confirm: Altered consciousness/toxidrome after suspected ingestion; identify the agent and toxidrome; assess ABCs and risk.
